name: Ezbon
overview: Ezbon was a male member of the tribe of Gad, known specifically as a son of Gad. He is mentioned among the sons of Israel who went to Egypt, highlighting his role in the early history of the Israelite people. He is also associated with the Oznites, a clan within the tribe of Gad, indicating his place within the tribal structure.
namesAndTitles: The name Ezbon appears as a proper name without a recorded meaning, simply identifying this individual in the genealogical records. He is also referred to as Ozni, which means "my ear" or "my hearing," reflecting a variant name within the same lineage.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ezbon was a son of Gad, establishing his direct paternal relationship. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are detailed in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Ezbon's significance lies in his inclusion among the sons of Israel who migrated to Egypt, a foundational event in the biblical narrative leading to the growth of the Israelite nation. His identification as a son of Gad situates him within one of the twelve tribes, contributing to the genealogical and tribal history important for understanding Israel's heritage. The mention of the Oznites connects him to a specific clan, emphasizing the detailed organization of Israelite families.
